rationale: The build job repeatedly fetches/installs Python dependencies across a large OS x Python-version matrix with no dependency cache. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache mechanism, reported benefit) and the measured fork experiment both support adding actions/cache@v4 for pip before installation. I added a cache step to the build job only, keyed by runner.os, matrix.python_version, and hashes of pyproject.toml plus dev-requirements.txt (the dependency inputs actually installed), so cache inputs track the environment and dependency files as the pattern requires. This only caches downloaded packages; it does not skip, reorder, or drop any lint/test/coverage step, so build and test coverage is preserved. No permissions are weakened, no secrets or privileged actions are added, and no new network access is introduced (pip already uses the network).
